title.narrative: PUBLIC AUDIT REFORM AND CAPACITY BUILDING OF OAGN

description.narrative: Objectives of the Grant. The main objective of the Grant is to help the Office of the Auditor General of Nepal (OAGN) to further enhance the institutional capacity to deliver quality public audit through (a) revising the existing audit guidelines according to the International Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions (INTOSAI) standardscomma the International Standards on Auditing (ISA) issued by the IFACcomma and the changes in Government rules and requirementscomma in the following public audit areas Revenue Auditcomma Procurement/ Public Works Auditcomma Project Audit and General Public Auditcomma (b) revising and consolidating the audit standards and guidelinescomma (c) improving the Auditor Generals reporting methodology commensurate with best international practicescomma and (d) developing the Human Resource Development Plan including the strengthening of its Training Division to create a strong and fully equipped training unit capable of providing quality training to its staff. To meet this objectivecomma the grant will help review the existing guidelines and develop new guidelines in the areas mentioned abovecomma and update audit standards and guidelines. In additioncomma it will help establish institutionalized training arrangements to implement the guidelines within OAGNcomma and conduct training programs. The grant will also help to provide exposure to senior officers through carefully plannedcomma monitoredcomma and evaluated programs of short term training secondment and training exchanges with well-developed Supreme Audit Institutes (SAIs) in South or East Asia or Pacific countriescomma and “twinning” with another successful SAI. These senior officers will be developed as “Trainers” who will then impart training to auditors responsible for the management of public audit. Background. The Nepal Country Assistance Strategy (CAS dated November 17comma 1998) identified governancecomma management of public expenditures and institutional constraints as serious impediments preventing Nepal from achieving its full economic potential and reducing poverty. In its Executive Summarycomma it specifies two new prongs: (a) bringing resources closer to the beneficiariescomma where they are most likely to be productively usedcomma and (b) fostering the strong governance needed to reduce waste and mismanagement. Good governancecomma public accountability and corruption control are stated to be high priorities of the Government. The Auditor General promotes and upholds the public accountabilitycomma credibility and discipline in financial operations. Quality audit helps to identify measures to eliminate or reduce waste and inefficiency in the mobilisation of public resourcescomma to create public awareness on good governancecomma to recommend the improvement of policies and procedurescomma and to sharpen the process of public accountability. Emerging changes in technology and growing demands from the public and donors for public accountability and good governance are putting pressure on the OAGN to be more proactivecomma quality conscious and oriented to serving the public interest. The technical assistance provided to date through the Banks past IDF grants has greatly contributed to the institutional development of OAGN. The first IDF grant helped to set up a stage for institutionalising the audit procedures and practices. The project contributed the five manuals which was immediately put in usecomma although they were implemented without field testing. A few policy decisions were made during the tenure of the project making departure from conservative approach to a more demand approach. The first IDF was rated “unsatisfactory” during exit. The second IDF grant was a follow on project which was deemed essential to carry on with the activities initiated during the first IDFcomma to continue to build the momentumcomma and to appreciate the Banks support to whatever marginal achievements were attempted. The project continued to focus in improving auditing of development projects and public enterprises comma and provide training to staff. Performance improved as compared to the first IDF. Outcomes achieved during the second IDF are becoming sustainable. It was rated “Partially Satisfactory” at exit. The third IDF which was provided to help OAG build a performance auditing capability as its contribution to improving the financial management of public sector projects was rated “Highly Satisfactory”. A strong commitment demonstrated by the Auditor General and ownership taken by him enabled to fully achieve the development objectives. Performance Audit Manual was developedcomma staff were trainedcomma twinning arrangement with Mala ysian OAG was arrangedcomma and performance auditing capacity has been internalised. In recognition of the fact that capacity building is an ongoing effortcomma it is important for the Bank to continue to be the development partner of OAGN to support its institutional development efforts. An added advantage is that the same Auditor General who implemented the third IDF is committed to continue reforms in auditing and improving the capability of his office. The recently completed Country Financial Accountability Assessment (CFAA dated July 5comma 2002) jointly carried out by His Majestys Government of Nepal (HMGN) and the World Bank confirmed that HMGN is serious and committed to improving public and private sector financial management. It has concluded that reforms in financial management are critical and should be approached in an integrated way covering planningcomma budgetingcomma accountingcomma internal controlcomma internal auditcomma external audit and oversight. With regard to public sector auditcomma the CFAA has recognized the strong and dedicated leadership of the OAGNcomma and has also concluded that the OAGN sets a good example of fearless reporting. A strong partnership forged by OAGN with the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) to follow-up on irregularities and other accountability issues is an impressive examplecomma as confirmed by the CFAA. While recognizing the OAGNs strong pointscomma the CFAA has made several recommendations to further enhance its capacity. HMGN has endorsed the recommendations of the CFAA and has committed to implement the Development Action Plan proposed therein. Recommendations related to public audit have been discussed and agreed with HMGN and OAGN. The CFAA recommended actions which includecomma inter aliacomma increasing OAGNs independencecomma providing sufficient resources to OAGN to cope with the needs for more trainingcomma equipmentcomma and expertisecomma reviewing and revising audit standards and guidelines according to INTOSAI standards and to accommodate changes in HMGN rulescomma developing Human Resource Development Plan including the strengthening of its training division to create a strong and fully equipped training unit capable of providing quality training to its staffcomma and providing exposure to senior officials of OAGN through carefully plannedcomma monitoredcomma and evaluated programs of short-term training secondment and training exchanges with well-developed SAIs abroad. The Auditor General requested the Banks IDF grant about a year back to support OAGN with its institutional development efforts. A draft proposal was submitted to the Bankcomma which was reviewed and discussed with OAGN. The Bank suggested that the OAGN should postpone this request until the CFAA was completedcomma and indicated that the Bank would be interested in providing support to the OAGN in line with the CFAA recommendations. The previous draft has been slightly modified along the lines of the CFAA recommendationscomma and this request is to support the specific action plans of CFAA to improve the quality of public audit. A few actions related to OAGN are already in the process of implementation as a result of strong commitment of the Auditor General. For examplecomma the long standing issue of repealing the Auditors Act 1974 to stop the licensing of auditors by the OAGNcomma and to pass this responsibility to the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nepal (ICAN)comma has recently been resolved after the endorsement by the Cabinet of the Auditor Generals proposal. The Auditor General has also agreed to arrange for an external peer review ofcomma and report oncomma its work at least once every two years by a reputable private audit firm. He has also agreed to have the OAGN accounts audited independently each year by a reputable private audit firm. Of the six specific CFAA recommendations to be implemented by the OAGNcomma two have already been implementedcomma a third related to the decentralization of the audit function by establishing OAGN field offices is under discussioncomma and the remaining three related to capacity building are expected to be implemented through the proposed IDF grant. All INTOSAI memberscomma including the OAG of Nepalcomma are expected to apply INTOSAI auditing standards. International Standards on Auditing (ISAs) issued by IFAC are very similar to INTOSAI standardscomma and efforts have been going on for some years to harmonize them as much as possible. The grant will be used to: (i) ensure that all OAGN auditing standards and guidelines comply with INTOSAI standards; (ii) review ISAs to identify any aspects representing an improvement on INTOSAI standards; and (iii) introduce any such improvement into OAG standards and guidelines. The Activities to be Financed Under the Grant. Include in the plan arrangements for in-house discussion series and inter-departmental seminars and discussions meetings in all stages of preparation of audit guidelines. wReview existing functionscomma policiescomma strategiescomma procedurescomma audit methodologycomma audit guidelines for revenuecomma procurement/public workscomma project accountscomma general public sector audit standardscomma and staffing of OAGNcomma in accordance with international best practices such as the INTOSAI standardscomma the International Standards on Auditing (ISA) issued by the IFACcomma and establish benchmarks on all these matterscomma in order to introduce appropriate reforms within OAGN. wRevise the existing audit guidelines according to INTOSAI standardscomma or the ISA (and also taking into consideration the changes in Government rules and requirements)comma in the following public sector audit areas Revenue Auditcomma Procurement/ Public Works Auditcomma Project Audit and other Public Sector Audit Procedures. wPilot the revised guidelines in a few selected development projects before official adoption. Finalize the audit guidelines both in English and in Nepali and officially adopt these guidelines. reportingcomma aiming to downsize the reporting volume. wPrepare a Human Resource Development Plan including the strengthening of OAGNs Training Division to create a strong and fully equipped training unit capable of providing quality training to its staff and capable of maintaining a good Training database. Provide exposure The purpose of the study tours is to provide exposure to senior officials to a well-developed SAI on how the audit guidelines are prepared comma how the training is conducted to staffcomma and how to present a succinct audit report; it will also provide exposure and skills on developing them as the Trainers who will take the responsibility to train other staff in OAG; the consulting firm will take responsibility to arrange the study tour program. to a selected group of senior officials Officials will include both senior and junior level officials having a combination of first classcomma second class and third class gazetted officials; a few of them will be developed as a trainer of OAGN (about 135 staff Number of officials proposed is 13comma but this figure may decrease or increase depending on the country which will be identified for the study tour as per the proposal of the consulting firmcomma within the limitation of the total budget allocated in the proposal.) through carefully plannedcomma monitoredcomma and evaluated programs of short-term training secondment and training exchanges in the above mentioned areas with well-developed SAIs in South or East Pacific countries and “twinning” with a successful SAI The bidder will be asked to indicate in the proposal the name of the SAI with which twinning arrangement will be made. (alsocomma assist the Steering Committee to develop transparent selection criteria to select candidates for exposure visit). These officials will be developed as “Trainers” who will be experts in developing annual training plan and imparting training to other audit staff. wDevelop a training toolkit (which should include audit methodologycomma reportingcomma quality control aspects etc.) in each audit area and train OAGN staff through formal class-room training and through on-the-job training in pilot auditscomma aiming to develop a network of expertise in each audit area. wUpgrade the computer skills of OAGN staff by providing training in Microsoft application programs (which include Wordcomma Excel and Access). wPrepare a project completion report providing details of work performed during the assignment correlating with each of the benchmarkscomma problems encountered and resolved and recommendations/proposals for ongoing efforts of OAGN in sustainable institutional development. Alsocomma include a supplementary feedback of the Steering Committee on the report on behalf of OAGN. In order to ensure the quality of audit guidelines and training toolkit and overall assessment of the work delivery under the programcomma the Supreme Audit Institution with which a twinning arrangement will be made will also be requested to send a senior official from the SAI to visit OAG Nepal towards the end of the program as part of the twinningcomma to review all the works carried out and provide a formal peer review as part of independent assessment on the quality of OAG work. Costs of the visit of the SAI official is built in as part of the international consultants visit; this requirement will be spelled out in the Request for Proposal. Likely Outcome of the Grant. The proposed activities to be financed under the grant will create the enabling environment to produce internationally recognized public sector auditing standardscomma and a better quality staff through a self-sustained staff training capacity within OAGN. All these are expected to result in a better quality audit by enhancing the oversight capacity of OAGN. This should also help to contain corruption and improve the efficiency with which public expenditures are managed. commacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacommacomma Relationship of Grant Proposal with Country Economic and Sector Work (or Business Plan) As stated abovecomma the Nepal Country Assistance Strategy (CAS dated November 17comma 1998) identified governancecomma public expenditure managementcomma corruption and overall institutional constraints as serious impediments preventing Nepal from achieving its full economic potential and reducing poverty. Actions identified in the CAS to move to a base case lending scenariocomma inter aliacomma included reducing delays in decision-makingcomma improving program implementation and adopting remedial measures to control misuse of funds and corruption. Upgrading the audit quality by revising the audit guidelines according to INTOSAI standards or the ISA and international best practicescomma preparing and implementing a Human Resource Development Plan in OAGNcomma and improving the skills of audit staffcomma would contribute to the realization of the above-mentioned CAS objectives. Alsocomma as explained in the last two paragraphs of the Background section abovecomma the activities proposed in this document for IDF grant financing are part of the CFAA Development Action Plan. Government Agency Responsible for Execution Office of the Auditor General of Nepal (OAGN) Government Contribution (Cash or In-Kind) US$ 58comma000 in Kind in form of staff costs and office space and in cash to cover required operating costs. Other Comments If Applicable None. Experience with the Implementation of Previous IDF Grants. OAGN has the experience of implementing three IDF Grants. The third IDF Grant was highly successful in terms of meeting the development objectives and accomplishing all targeted activitiescomma as a result of experience gained through the implementation of the first two IDF grants which were not so successful. A high degree of ownership and commitment by OAGN in program implementation of the third IDF is a major factor leading to success. Based on previous experiencecomma and with a strong and dedicated leadership of the Auditor Generalcomma implementation of the proposed grant is expected to be fully owned and managed by OAGN in accordance with its institutional needs and with a determination to continue to improve the audit quality by means of revisions in guidelines and by upgrading the skills of staff through sustainable and institutionalised training programs. In the context of the recent Nepal Development Forum and the CFAA discussionscomma the Government and OAGN reaffirmed their commitment to moving ahead for instituting good governance and improved financial accountability. In view of the many strong points noted abovecomma the risk of not attaining the set objectives is very low.
